goAhead: add solid fixes/implementations until s2 is completed. including the previous gaps etc. so when you're done i should be ready to start s3.

groups.note: Format assertion on library-only routes and the request-time use of the compile-time regexp cache. CC-01 is a process crash: do this first.
$recursiveRef and $recursiveAnchor as first-class references, with the class backstop shared with GC-02.
The walk mirrors exactly which positions the library compiles, with which base and in which order (decision 24: no new refusal).
Deterministic memory measurements replace every sampled peak, before any later class adds memory tests.
One walk-time compile budget of 1 MiB with byte terms (GC-03) and count terms (GC-09) (decision 20).
Non-canonical indexes accepted as aliases; repeat counts and seen sets keyed by the decoded value (decision 21).
Clamp the eight integer keywords above 2^63-1 in a compiled copy; presence kept apart from value (decision 22).
Regex parser work the lexical pass does not count.
Charge anchor-name bytes and the decision wrapper frames (decision 24).
Regexp matcher costs from the compiled program, add() depth charged, and an absolute 128 MiB stack ceiling with 413 above it (decision 23).
Kept memory figures, the number model at the library actual parse sites, and values outside the decoder data model through the exported API.
Pin every walk rule and resolution mirror per keyword, form and route, and prove every work-model term with a test a mutation fails.

Decode config.schema with the configuration own depth limit (decision 25) and bound the raw decode before it (GC-10); keyword locations per error kind; deterministic compile diagnostics; document and pin the library deviations (decision 24). Also round-9 minors 2 and 4 in runs/w3-s2-wp51-r9.json, which no class covers: close them as that record describes.

minors.where: internal/config/schemaview/schemaview.go:21-33 (package doc); contract internal/config/diag Path.String / List.Sort (WP-01), schemaidx.ItemElem (WP-28), 01 req 48
minors.issue: A downstream cost still grows with errors times element size, and it sits outside WP-35's code. The 10,000 diagnostics Validate returns are cheap to build now. Rendering them is not. On the finding's listener input (32 KiB name, 20k hostnames, 162 KB), diag.List.Sort allocates 958 MB in 1.8 s and diag.WriteText allocates 393 MB, because each path re-renders the 32 KiB key. A 1 MB key would push that into tens of GB, so the end-to-end `ruralz bundle validate` / activation path remains exposed. The package doc states this correctly. The engineer says contract change requests to WP-01 and WP-28, with an OQ on 01 req 48, were raised, but the report reached me truncated, so I could not verify their text.
minors.fix: Make sure the contract change requests to WP-01 (diag.Path rendering, List.Sort comparing rendered paths) and WP-28 (ItemElem size), and the OQ row on 01 req 48, are actually filed and tracked. One option is a bounded or truncated rendering of large keys and items, with List.Sort comparing paths element by element. No change is needed in schemaview.

minors.issue: Nothing guards the performance of the long-segment common-prefix memo. TestComparePaths only checks that some pair was memoized. If the memo were removed, sorting entries below two sibling elements that share a long prefix would cost errors times segment length in CPU, and that would not show in TotalAlloc. So TestLargePathElements would still pass. Today the memo works: in a probe with 2 listeners whose 64 KiB names share a prefix, 10k errors each and positions stripped, mapping took 142 ms with 1 memoized pair.
minors.fix: Optional: count commonPrefix bytes, or memo misses, in the memo, the same way memo.read counts reads, and bound that count in a stripped-positions case with two large siblings and many errors below each.

minors.where: internal/config/overlay/merge.go:183-227 (mergeMap dispatch) and overlay.go:171-176; 01 req 25; FuzzOverlay property
minors.issue: A base `$patch` can still reach a clean result with no diagnostic. A base Policy of type validation.json-schema may legally hold `$patch` as data inside config.schema, and CheckBase rightly exempts it. An overlay that changes only spec.type to an open config type, such as `{"spec":{"type":"cors"}}` or `plugin`, moves that value into free content. The result keeps `$patch` at spec.config.schema.$patch and Apply reports nothing. FuzzOverlay's own properties fail on this reachable input: the second pipeline pass reports RZ-CFG-006, so the idempotency check fails, and strayPatch finds the member. I confirmed this with a probe that copies the fuzz body (base `{"kind":"Policy","spec":{"type":"validation.json-schema","config":{"schema":{"$patch":1}}}}`, overlay `{"spec":{"type":"cors"}}`). A 90 s fuzz run did not hit it, but nightly long runs can.
minors.fix: After merging an existing resource in Apply, check the merged tree for `$patch` outside a JSONSchemaDocument value. Report RZ-CFG-005, for example at the overlay spec.type, with a message saying the base value is no longer a JSON Schema document. CheckBase's walk can be reused on the merged root with a CodeSchema code. Alternatively, keep the behavior and narrow FuzzOverlay's idempotency and stray checks to exclude it, with a documented reason. Either way, add this input as a FuzzOverlay seed.

minors.issue: The new skip for variable-sourced values also skips values taken from an authored default. A headers `set[]` entry `{name: authorization, value: "${X:-hunter2}"}` with X unset resolves to `hunter2`, which is written in the Bundle. Before the fix it got the credential-header RZ-CFG-013 warning; now it gets none, because scalar() records X in Vars even when the default was used. Confirmed by probe. Separately, `${AUTH_TOKEN}` whose value matches a detector (for example `Bearer <24 chars>`) still gets two RZ-CFG-013 warnings on one scalar, the detector warning and the secret-like name warning. walker.warn says 'one RZ-CFG-013 warning per scalar', but the secret-like warning bypasses that dedupe. Req 30 does require the per-use warning, so this second point is cosmetic.
minors.fix: In scalar(), record whether any expression took its `:-` default, and run the header-literal check when a default supplied the text. Skip it only when every expression resolved from the variable source. Add a TestCredentialWarnings case for `${X:-hunter2}`. Optionally either reword warn's doc comment to say secret-like warnings are per use, or skip the detector warning for a scalar that already got a secret-like warning.

minors.where: internal/config/defaults/chunk.go:39-42,63-66 (an interface target is always decoded whole) and decode.go:39-44; 01 req 53 (remainder of earlier minor finding 3)
minors.issue: Most of the time-based yield fix holds, but Decode still runs a single encoding/json call for large values at interface (any) positions. These are the member values of v1alpha1.PluginConfig (map[string]any) and of Plugin spec.configSchema (map[string]any). JSONSchemaDocument.UnmarshalJSON is a similar case: it runs json.Valid over the whole inline schema between two timer reads. I probed with go test -overlay, using an instrumented copy of work.go that records the longest gap between two check() calls; no repo files were touched. A plugin Policy config {"x": [12,000 small objects]} and a Plugin configSchema of the same size each ran about 31 ms between timer reads, inside one whole() encoding/json call. A validation.json-schema enum of 30,000 strings ran about 0.5 ms inside unmarshaler(). Typed shapes behave as intended: the 12,000-label, 12,000-endpoint Upstream had a longest gap of 0.4 ms. Two statements are therefore not true for plugin configs and configSchema: the package doc's 'Large values are decoded in pieces of at most 256 nodes', and the claim in the report that Decode is split. With a large source, one any-valued member can run for hundreds of milliseconds without yielding.
minors.fix: Split interface targets in the chunker. When the target is a nil interface and the node is a KindMap or KindList, build a map[string]any or []any directly. Decode each member or element through c.decode into a fresh any value, and set the result into the interface. Leaves give exactly what encoding/json with UseNumber gives: json.Number, string, bool, or nil. Add a plugin-config case and a Plugin configSchema case to TestChunkedDecodeSplits and TestChunkedDecodeEqualsWhole. For JSONSchemaDocument, accept the json.Valid cost and document it in the package comment and in chunker's doc. pkg/ is not WP-37's to change, so if that cost matters, raise a request against the pkg owner.

minors.issue: The switch to comparing allocated bytes removed the wall-clock dependence, but the test can no longer see the regression class its own comment names: 'a per-member Get, Select or ItemElem would make stage G quadratic'. Those scans allocate nothing. I probed with an overlay that added `_, _ = n.Get(m.Key)` per member to normalizer.visit. BenchmarkScale then reported labels at 4.6 ms for 1,500 members and 234 ms for 12,000 (51x for 8x the members); open config members and json schema document showed the same. TestScaleLinear still passed, with byte ratios of 7.7 to 8.4. As written, it guards only against per-member copies, paths and indexes.
minors.fix: Make the comment accurate: it detects per-member allocation, not scans. Back it with a measure that does not depend on the machine and that counts the stage's own lookups. For example, send the stage's per-member Get, Select and ItemElem calls through a small helper that increments a counter on work (only Run-local state, so no package-level variables), and assert that counter scales by about 8x. Alternatively, have internal/tool/benchgate enforce the BenchmarkScale n:8n ratio.

minors.where: 02 req 19 / docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md (contract change request from earlier major finding 1)
minors.issue: The code fix is complete. Normalize reports RZ-CFG-005 at every KindNull, Resource returns nil, and FuzzStageIdempotent asserts that an accepted tree holds no null. This makes a user-visible restriction: JSON Schema documents in validation.json-schema configs and Plugin configSchema can no longer contain null literals such as "default": null, "const": null or "enum": [..., null], and plugin configs can no longer carry null values. Neither docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md nor stage F says so. The relayed engineer report is cut off, so I could not confirm that the requested contract change request was actually raised.
minors.fix: Confirm that the engineer's report raises the contract change request. Doc 02 and stage F (schemaview) should state that null is rejected in free content and in inline or plugin JSON Schema documents in M1, or else define a representation for null. Record it as an OQ-configuration-model-<n> row if it is not settled.

minors.where: internal/config/precedence/precedence.go:62-63, locate.go:9, resolve.go:17, rows.go:13 (architecture 1.2 row for config/precedence)
minors.issue: The package imports internal/config/tree (for Options.Files and to walk hub.Resource.Tree) and pkg/config/v1alpha1. Neither is in its 1.2 'May import' list, which names config/hub, config/registry, config/diag, phase and expr. Both are lower layers and create no cycle, and depguard does not enforce the row, so lint passes. It still breaks the rule that a package imports 'only those its row in 1.2 lists'.
minors.fix: Send a contract change request to add config/tree and v1alpha1 to the config/precedence row in 1.2 (the package cannot avoid either: hub.Object returns *v1alpha1 types and hub.Resource.Tree is a *tree.Node). Mention it in the WP report.

minors.issue: Resolve calls Options.Body.ReferencesRequestBody from several worker goroutines (selectAll on the forEach pool), but the Options doc never says the oracle must be safe for concurrent use. expr.Compiler is documented as safe, so production callers are fine. A custom oracle, such as a test stub or a future wrapper, that is not safe would race without any warning.
minors.fix: Add to the Options.Body doc: 'Body must be safe for concurrent use: Resolve calls it from up to workers goroutines.'

minors.issue: Rows builds its own registry.New() to find the Filter class of a removed Policy that has no materialized filterClass. It ignores the registry the Resolver was built with, so a Resolver made with a non-default registry could print a different class for removed rows than for live entries. After stage G this path is effectively dead, because filterClass is always materialized.
minors.fix: Use only the materialized p.Spec.FilterClass and leave FilterClass empty otherwise, or make Rows a method on *Resolver (or pass the registry in) so live and removed rows use one registry.

minors.issue: TestScale uses time.Now and time.Since. They only feed t.Logf, but architecture section 0 item 4 says time.Now appears only in clock.Real, and tests must not depend on wall-clock time. The test also claims the run 'stays linear' without asserting it.
minors.fix: Remove the timing log, or use b.Elapsed in a benchmark. If linearity matters, assert an allocation or operation count instead of time.

minors.issue: BenchmarkResolve's Bundle has no positioned trees and no FileTable, so the locator path is never measured. In the pipeline, the per-entry tree walk and the FileTable mutex taken on every Location call (tree.FileTable.Location locks t.mu) run for every attachment. The 5,000-Route figure (about 35 ms/op) therefore understates the real stage I cost and hides lock contention between workers.
minors.fix: Give the benchmark Bundle Gateway, Route and Upstream trees (as listTree does in scale_test.go) and pass a FileTable in Options, so the 02 section 6 benchmark covers the production path.

minors.issue: The property checks soundness only: a locked Policy is never removed, and no RZ-CFG-019 is raised for excluding an overridable Policy. It does not check completeness: that every exclusion or same-slot replacement of an attached overridable:false Gateway Policy raises RZ-CFG-019. It also never checks the one-Policy-per-slot law on each Upstream leg, only on the client leg. If either broke, for example 019 being dropped on replace, the fuzz target would not catch it (the unit tests and fixtures still would).
minors.fix: For each Route, compute the attached locked Gateway Policies and assert one RZ-CFG-019 for every excludePolicies entry naming one and for every resolved, scope-valid Route entry in its slot. Run the same slot-uniqueness check over every c.Legs[i].Phases.

minors.issue: If the content has an unknown top-level member and its `format` member is missing or not a string, Decode returns RZ-CFG-027 instead of RZ-CFG-024. For example, `{"formatVersion":2,"resources":[]}` gives RZ-CFG-027 "no format member", and `{"format":1,"resources":[],"level":2}` gives RZ-CFG-027 too (both confirmed with a scratch test). The `newer` findings are collected first, but the format nil/non-string checks return before anything looks at them. This breaks 02 req 33 ("a top-level member other than format and resources" is RZ-CFG-024) and the package's own rule that a newer producer wins over a form problem (TestDecodePrecedence). The resource level already gets this order right.
minors.fix: In envelope(), once the members are scanned, return fail(CodeNewer, nil, newer...) when len(newer) > 0, before the `format == nil` and `format.Kind != tree.KindString` checks. Add both inputs above to TestDecodeNewer or TestDecodePrecedence.

minors.issue: A zero revision.Revision (empty Content) makes AppendDump write invalid JSON: `{"content":,"digest":"sha256:000...","revision":"rev-000000000000"}` (confirmed). The doc comment says a Node without a Revision has no dump, but nothing enforces that. The handler is wired later (WP-76) and could serve a malformed 200 body before the first activation.
minors.fix: Make the precondition hard to miss: return dst unchanged (or an ok bool) when len(active.Content) == 0, or panic with a clear message. Also state in the doc comment that the injected handler must answer without calling AppendDump when no snapshot is published. Add a test for the zero case.

minors.issue: Production code imports config/schemaidx, internal/errcode and pkg/config/v1alpha1. The architecture's May-import row for config/canonical lists only config/tree, config/hub, config/revision, config/diag and jsonval. The schemaidx import is needed: 02 reqs 23 and 33 need the schema, and spec 02 section 3 defines NewEncoder(idx *schemaidx.Index). No lint rule fails, but the package table is out of step with the code.
minors.fix: No code change. Ask the lead for a contract change: add config/schemaidx, errcode and v1alpha1 to the config/canonical row of the section 1.2 table.

minors.where: engineer report, requirements; internal/config/canonical/*_test.go; 02 test plan 26 and req 34
minors.issue: The report says 02 test plan item 26 (secret leak) is implemented, but no test in the package uses a canary value or checks that a resolved secret is absent. The only evidence for req 34 (secretRef written as references) is the shop golden file.
minors.fix: Add a test that calls t.Setenv("RURALZ_STATE_STORE_URL", canary), writes a `file` secret holding a canary, encodes a Gateway whose stateStore.url and TLS use those secretRefs, and asserts the canaries appear in neither Encode's Content nor AppendDump's output while the secretRef objects do. Otherwise, drop item 26 from the claim.

minors.issue: Decoder.Verify on the 5,749-resource Revision measured 51-57 ms/op here, with 25 MB and 141,743 allocations per op (the host was loaded: load average 8 on 4 cores). Workers=2 gave no speedup. A CPU profile shows the sequential parse at about 31% cumulative (parser.object/array/value) plus about 20% GC. The target is not met or demonstrated; the engineer disclosed this.
minors.fix: Treat this as a follow-up and record it in the WP report. Cut per-node allocations: take member and item slices from slabs as nodes are, and resolve positions lazily from offsets instead of calling Locator.Position per token. Then re-measure on an idle host.

minors.issue: The golden bytes and digests encode the parsed trees before stage G: no defaults are materialized and scalars are not normalized (for example `"maxRequestBodyBytes":"10Mi"`). shop.digest is therefore not the Revision of the configuration model's shop-bundle. The test comment explains this, but the file names invite misuse as the real golden digest that WP-75 will pin.
minors.fix: Rename the files to show they hold the encoder over parsed trees (for example shop.parsed.json and shop.parsed.digest), or add a one-line testdata README. Make sure WP-75 owns the post-stage-G shop-bundle goldens (02 req 79).

minors.issue: Content that uses an enum value or Policy type this release does not know (for example `spec.type: "future.type"`) passes Decode. Dispatch does not match, the config is open, and stage F later reports RZ-CFG-005, not RZ-CFG-024. Every Policy config in the rendered schema is open (no additionalProperties: false), so unknown config members from a newer release are also accepted as open content. This follows the spec's literal list (fields and kinds only), but a Last-Known-Good written by a newer release with a new Policy type will show RZ-CFG-005 rather than the skew code.
minors.fix: Do not invent behavior. Record an OQ in spec 02 section 9 (or ask the lead) on whether an unknown enum or dispatch value in canonical content should be RZ-CFG-024. If adopted, report it in the newer walk where the instance value is not in Node.Enum().
